title: brand-aware iconography & interaction tokens for high-contrast dark themes
creator: Lina Patel
description: Goal: establish a consistent system for adapting iconography, focus/hover interaction tokens, and chart palettes across brand themes in high-contrast dark mode. This ticket focuses on token mappings and component-level overrides that preserve brand color identity while meeting accessibility contrast thresholds and keeping component visuals consistent with surface elevation rules. Deliverables: 1) token mapping sheet (light <-> dark, default <-> brand variants), 2) component override spec for Button, Table, Chart, and Icon components, 3) engineering-ready CSS/Token examples for runtime theming and runtime fallback behavior, 4) automated visual tests and accessibility checklist.
comments: 2025-02-16 — Lina Patel: Initial spec drafted; added goals and deliverables. Highlighted three open questions: (1) strictness of brand hue preservation vs. contrast boosts, (2) icon monochrome vs. colored accents in dense UI, (3) how chart palettes should adapt for semantic coloring.

2025-02-18 — Marco Rossi: Did a quick feasibility review with frontend. Runtime can accept an optional 'brand-contrast' token override map; engineering prefers a flattened token set for faster lookups. We'll provide a flattened token example and a migration guide.

2025-02-21 — Accessibility review (Jamal Nguyen): Recommend minimum 4.5:1 for primary action text on interactive surfaces. For decorative icons, ensure discernibility when used as affordances (>=3:1) and provide ARIA alternatives.

2025-02-25 — Design critique (Ava Chen): Reworked icon accent rules — propose 'accent-on-dark' tokens that are desaturated variants of brand colors to avoid spectral vibrancy on OLED; added examples for warning/error brand themes.

2025-02-28 — Engineering feedback (Priya Kapoor): Confirmed ability to map chart gradients using two tokens (chart-foreground-1, chart-foreground-2) per semantic color. Asked for explicit hexs for 3 breakpoints per brand for graceful fallbacks.

2025-03-01 — Marco Rossi: Implemented token fixtures in branch theming/brand-icon-tokens, created unit tests for Button hover/focus contrast. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/1297

2025-03-02 — Lina Patel: Logged visual QA tasks and checklist; scheduling cross-team review with Platform UI and Observability (Charts) next week. Added 'zebra-stripe' guidelines for tables in dark-high-contrast where stripe colors must be < 3% luminance difference to avoid pattern noise.
2025-03-02 — Review note (Diego Morales): Please include sample token usage for 'compact' density variants and ensure icons used in table cells still meet touch-target cues in mobile breakpoints.
implementation_notes: Provide a CSV token mapping: token_name, light_hex, dark_hex, brand_variant_hex, contrast_delta_hint
Chart palettes: export 3-step gradients per semantic color and an alternate high-contrast pair
Component overrides should fall back to core tokens when brand tokens missing; runtime should log missing mappings in staging
Add visual regression snapshots in Percy for Button, Table rows, and Charts across Default + 3 brand themes in both light and dark
acceptance_criteria: Spec file (docs) with token mapping CSV uploaded and linked from ticket
Figma frames with examples for Button, Table, Icon, and Chart in Default, Brand-A, Brand-B in both light and dark
Engineering PR that wires token fixtures to the runtime and includes visual tests
Accessibility audit confirming interactive text/button contrast >= 4.5:1 and icons used as affordances >= 3:1
Rollout plan documenting incremental enablement by customer/org and fallback logging behavior
